Kessendorf — the Hospice of Saint Ildra the Merciful
trans-unit.note: Place and time caption at the top-left of the scene.

trans-unit.source: An old surgeon’s woodcut hangs by the hospice door: a man stuck with every blade, bolt and fang in the world — and standing.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "prologue" (Kessendorf — the Hospice of Saint Ildra the Merciful), line 1 of 14.

trans-unit.source: Beneath it, in faded ink: “Here is the battlefield. Hold it.”
trans-unit.note: Story scene "prologue" (Kessendorf — the Hospice of Saint Ildra the Merciful), line 2 of 14.

trans-unit.source: The Free City of Kessendorf. Winter, in the ninth year of the Long Muster.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "prologue" (Kessendorf — the Hospice of Saint Ildra the Merciful), line 3 of 14.

trans-unit.source: The river has frozen twice. The pyres outside the east gate have not gone out since autumn.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "prologue" (Kessendorf — the Hospice of Saint Ildra the Merciful), line 4 of 14.

trans-unit.source: So. You are the new sawbones the Guild sent me. Kreuzer, is it?
trans-unit.note: Story scene "prologue" (Kessendorf — the Hospice of Saint Ildra the Merciful), line 5 of 14.

trans-unit.source: Apothecary-surgeon, sworn at Weissburg. I have my letters, Master Haller—
trans-unit.note: Story scene "prologue" (Kessendorf — the Hospice of Saint Ildra the Merciful), line 6 of 14.

trans-unit.source: Letters. Letters don’t stop a man bleeding into the straw. Hands do. Show me your hands.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "prologue" (Kessendorf — the Hospice of Saint Ildra the Merciful), line 7 of 14.

trans-unit.source: …Steady enough. Why would a sworn Weissburg man take a charity bed in a city that burns its sick?
trans-unit.note: Story scene "prologue" (Kessendorf — the Hospice of Saint Ildra the Merciful), line 8 of 14.

trans-unit.source: Weissburg taught me the rules, Master. I came somewhere too poor to afford them.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "prologue" (Kessendorf — the Hospice of Saint Ildra the Merciful), line 9 of 14.

trans-unit.source: Hm. Sister! Our young doctor has arrived just in time for the Tuesday knife-fights.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "prologue" (Kessendorf — the Hospice of Saint Ildra the Merciful), line 10 of 14.

trans-unit.source: Sister Ilse, of the Merciful Order. I keep the instruments, the ledgers, and the Master’s temper.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "prologue" (Kessendorf — the Hospice of Saint Ildra the Merciful), line 11 of 14.

trans-unit.source: There’s a drover on the table already. Somebody at the Crooked Goose disagreed with his dice.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "prologue" (Kessendorf — the Hospice of Saint Ildra the Merciful), line 12 of 14.

trans-unit.source: Knife wounds. Simple work. I’ll watch.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "prologue" (Kessendorf — the Hospice of Saint Ildra the Merciful), line 13 of 14.

trans-unit.source: And Kreuzer — in this hospice we do not lose patients to simple work.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "prologue" (Kessendorf — the Hospice of Saint Ildra the Merciful), line 14 of 14.

trans-unit.source: The Hospice — the next morning
trans-unit.note: Place and time caption at the top-left of the scene.

trans-unit.source: The next morning the Watch arrives before the bread does.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-2" (The Hospice — the next morning), line 1 of 9.

trans-unit.source: Make way! Make way, damn you! Surgeon! Where’s the surgeon?
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-2" (The Hospice — the next morning), line 2 of 9.

trans-unit.source: Captain Mauer of the Watch. Lower your voice, Captain, this is a house of mercy.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-2" (The Hospice — the next morning), line 3 of 9.

trans-unit.source: Twelve went out with the timber-road caravan. Twelve came back, eleven walking. Horned folk hit us at dawn.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-2" (The Hospice — the next morning), line 4 of 9.

trans-unit.source: Young Pieter took a shaft in the side. Twelve, Doctor. I’d like it to stay twelve.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-2" (The Hospice — the next morning), line 5 of 9.

trans-unit.source: Then put him down gently, Captain, and stop counting him among the dead.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-2" (The Hospice — the next morning), line 6 of 9.

trans-unit.source: Horned-folk heads are barbed like fish-hooks. They cut a notch in their antlers for every one that sticks in a man.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-2" (The Hospice — the next morning), line 7 of 9.

trans-unit.source: Rip it straight out and you’ll take half his side with it. Free the barbs first, then pull. Cleanly.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-2" (The Hospice — the next morning), line 8 of 9.

trans-unit.source: Twelve. Say it with me, Doctor. Twelve.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-2" (The Hospice — the next morning), line 9 of 9.

trans-unit.source: The Hospice — noon
trans-unit.note: Place and time caption at the top-left of the scene.

trans-unit.source: Noon. A second sack of turnips arrives at the gate. The drover has told his friends about us.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-3" (The Hospice — noon), line 1 of 8.

trans-unit.source: Doctor, the gunsmiths’ quarter. An apprentice was proving a new handgun barrel and it burst in his hands.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-3" (The Hospice — noon), line 2 of 8.

trans-unit.source: Burns across the chest, lead driven under the skin — and a note from the Gunsmiths’ Guild pinned to his shirt.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-3" (The Hospice — noon), line 3 of 8.

trans-unit.source: The Guild will pay for his care. Once we have paid the Guild’s fee for inspecting its own burst barrel.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-3" (The Hospice — noon), line 4 of 8.

trans-unit.source: Naturally. In Kessendorf a man pays the Guild for the privilege of being shot by its work.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-3" (The Hospice — noon), line 5 of 8.

trans-unit.source: Then we send the Guild a bill for the lead we take out of him. Itemised, by the ounce.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-3" (The Hospice — noon), line 6 of 8.

trans-unit.source: Powder burns. The black crust is dead meat: off with it before any salve, or it festers underneath.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-3" (The Hospice — noon), line 7 of 8.

trans-unit.source: The shot is deep. You’ll open him along the line I’ve inked. And if his pulse flags — the tincture.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-3" (The Hospice — noon), line 8 of 8.

trans-unit.source: The Hospice — dusk
trans-unit.note: Place and time caption at the top-left of the scene.

trans-unit.source: Word travels fast in Kessendorf. By dusk, there is a queue at the hospice door.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-4" (The Hospice — dusk), line 1 of 10.

trans-unit.source: This one was found in the Tanners’ Rows. Swellings at the neck and groin. Fever. Maggots in an old sore.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-4" (The Hospice — dusk), line 2 of 10.

trans-unit.source: Matthis Kolb. Twenty years a tanner’s man. Write that, Sister, not “vagrant”. I had a trade before I had a fever.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-4" (The Hospice — dusk), line 3 of 10.

trans-unit.source: Matthis Kolb, tanner’s man. Written, and underlined.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-4" (The Hospice — dusk), line 4 of 10.

trans-unit.source: Buboes, and a rotting sore. He’s slept in the Rows among the hides. Burn the grubs, Kreuzer — not the man.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-4" (The Hospice — dusk), line 5 of 10.

trans-unit.source: Nobody hears the door. There is simply a man in black standing in the ward, where a moment ago there was not.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-4" (The Hospice — dusk), line 6 of 10.

trans-unit.source: A plague case. In the city. How very interesting.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-4" (The Hospice — dusk), line 7 of 10.

trans-unit.source: …Inquisitor Stroh. Of the Ash Tribunal.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-4" (The Hospice — dusk), line 8 of 10.

trans-unit.source: Carry on, Doctor. I only wish to watch. Pestilence so often has a sponsor — and I hear the Kilnrows are coughing too.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-4" (The Hospice — dusk), line 9 of 10.

trans-unit.source: Then stand back from the table, Inquisitor. Whoever sponsors it, it isn’t particular whom it takes.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-4" (The Hospice — dusk), line 10 of 10.

trans-unit.source: The Hospice — the small hours
trans-unit.note: Place and time caption at the top-left of the scene.

trans-unit.source: Near midnight a carriage stops at the gate. Its door panel has been planed smooth where a crest should be — on purpose.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-5" (The Hospice — the small hours), line 1 of 8.

trans-unit.source: The choir… they’re singing in me… make them stop singing…
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-5" (The Hospice — the small hours), line 2 of 8.

trans-unit.source: Doctor, look at his chest. Those marks — they’re moving. That one is an eye, with a stroke drawn through it.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-5" (The Hospice — the small hours), line 3 of 8.

trans-unit.source: …That is no disease. Those are sigils. Someone has written on this boy.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-5" (The Hospice — the small hours), line 4 of 8.

trans-unit.source: Then we unwrite him. The brand, Sister. And more light.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-5" (The Hospice — the small hours), line 5 of 8.

trans-unit.source: If something answers when you do — there is an old apothecary’s rite. The Litany of Stillness.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-5" (The Hospice — the small hours), line 6 of 8.

trans-unit.source: Draw the five-pointed star and still your heart. For a few breaths, the world will wait for you.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-5" (The Hospice — the small hours), line 7 of 8.

trans-unit.source: Do not do it where the Inquisitor can see. The Tribunal does not distinguish between a prayer and a spell.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-5" (The Hospice — the small hours), line 8 of 8.

trans-unit.source: The Hospice — before dawn
trans-unit.note: Place and time caption at the top-left of the scene.

trans-unit.source: The thing in the boy’s chest came apart like wet ash. The boy sleeps. He no longer hears singing.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-end" (The Hospice — before dawn), line 1 of 13.

trans-unit.source: Doctor… after it broke, a word was left seared into the flesh. Matins. And beside it, fading: the struck-through eye.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-end" (The Hospice — before dawn), line 2 of 13.

trans-unit.source: The first of the canonical hours. The first prayer of the night.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-end" (The Hospice — before dawn), line 3 of 13.

trans-unit.source: A curse that lives and fights like a beast, and signs itself like a psalm. A Malison.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-end" (The Hospice — before dawn), line 4 of 13.

trans-unit.source: And if this was Matins… then somewhere, someone is already writing Lauds.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-end" (The Hospice — before dawn), line 5 of 13.

trans-unit.source: In the yard, the carriage without a crest pulls away before anyone thinks to ask whose it is.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-end" (The Hospice — before dawn), line 6 of 13.

trans-unit.source: A remarkable recovery, Doctor. Remarkable.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-end" (The Hospice — before dawn), line 7 of 13.

trans-unit.source: Tell me — at the end, your hands moved so very quickly. Almost as if time itself were… obliging you.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-end" (The Hospice — before dawn), line 8 of 13. Variant line: shown only if the Litany was spoken in the preceding operation.

trans-unit.source: Practice, Inquisitor. And the grace of Saint Ildra.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-end" (The Hospice — before dawn), line 9 of 13. Variant line: shown only if the Litany was spoken in the preceding operation.

trans-unit.source: Of course. The grace of the Saint. I shall pray on it.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-end" (The Hospice — before dawn), line 10 of 13. Variant line: shown only if the Litany was spoken in the preceding operation.

trans-unit.source: I watched every stroke. No tricks, no prayers. Only a surgeon, working. I find it almost disappointing.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-end" (The Hospice — before dawn), line 11 of 13. Variant line: shown only if the Litany was NOT spoken in the preceding operation.

trans-unit.source: Surgery usually is, Inquisitor. That is how you know it worked.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-end" (The Hospice — before dawn), line 12 of 13. Variant line: shown only if the Litany was NOT spoken in the preceding operation.

trans-unit.source: END OF CHAPTER I — THE HOUR OF MATINS
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s1-end" (The Hospice — before dawn), line 13 of 13.

trans-unit.source: The Hospice — after the knife-work
trans-unit.note: Place caption of aftermath scene after op1-1 "a1-1".

trans-unit.source: The drover lives. He pays in turnips and a promise not to gamble again. He will break it by Friday.
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op1-1 "a1-1" (The Hospice — after the knife-work), line 1 of 6.

trans-unit.source: Clean. Quick. Hm. Don’t let it go to your head, Kreuzer. It was simple work.
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op1-1 "a1-1" (The Hospice — after the knife-work), line 2 of 6. Variant line: shown only if the preceding operation's rank was high (high = XS/S, mid = A/B, low = C).

trans-unit.source: Adequate. The Weissburg Guild would call that adequate. I call it Tuesday.
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op1-1 "a1-1" (The Hospice — after the knife-work), line 3 of 6. Variant line: shown only if the preceding operation's rank was mid (high = XS/S, mid = A/B, low = C).

trans-unit.source: He’ll live. Eventually. I said simple work, Kreuzer. I did not say leisurely.
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op1-1 "a1-1" (The Hospice — after the knife-work), line 4 of 6. Variant line: shown only if the preceding operation's rank was low (high = XS/S, mid = A/B, low = C).

trans-unit.source: Turnips, Sister?
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op1-1 "a1-1" (The Hospice — after the knife-work), line 5 of 6.

trans-unit.source: Under “fees, vegetable”. We have a column. It is the longest one in the ledger.
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op1-1 "a1-1" (The Hospice — after the knife-work), line 6 of 6.

trans-unit.source: The Hospice — after the barbed shaft
trans-unit.note: Place caption of aftermath scene after op1-2 "a1-2".

trans-unit.source: Pieter will keep his side, and his opinion of the horned folk.
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op1-2 "a1-2" (The Hospice — after the barbed shaft), line 1 of 4.

trans-unit.source: Twelve. Twelve walking. The Watch pays its debts, Doctor. Slowly, but it pays.
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op1-2 "a1-2" (The Hospice — after the barbed shaft), line 2 of 4.

trans-unit.source: You nicked those barbs like a tailor. Where did Weissburg find the time to teach you that?
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op1-2 "a1-2" (The Hospice — after the barbed shaft), line 3 of 4. Variant line: shown only if the preceding operation's rank was high (high = XS/S, mid = A/B, low = C).

trans-unit.source: You tore him on the second barb. He will heal. He will also remember you.
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op1-2 "a1-2" (The Hospice — after the barbed shaft), line 4 of 4. Variant line: shown only if the preceding operation's rank was low (high = XS/S, mid = A/B, low = C).

trans-unit.source: The Hospice — after the burst barrel
trans-unit.note: Place caption of aftermath scene after op1-3 "a1-3".

trans-unit.source: Anno keeps both hands. The Guild keeps its fee. Nobody keeps the barrel.
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op1-3 "a1-3" (The Hospice — after the burst barrel), line 1 of 4.

trans-unit.source: His master called. He asked whether the lead we took out of the boy could be melted down again.
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op1-3 "a1-3" (The Hospice — after the burst barrel), line 2 of 4.

trans-unit.source: Tell him yes. Tell him it is the best-proven lead in Kessendorf.
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op1-3 "a1-3" (The Hospice — after the burst barrel), line 3 of 4.

trans-unit.source: The boy will scar. Burns remember every minute you wasted, Kreuzer. So do I.
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op1-3 "a1-3" (The Hospice — after the burst barrel), line 4 of 4. Variant line: shown only if the preceding operation's rank was low (high = XS/S, mid = A/B, low = C).

trans-unit.source: The Hospice — after dark
trans-unit.note: Place caption of aftermath scene after op1-4 "a1-4".

trans-unit.source: Matthis Kolb sleeps in a clean bed for the first time in a year. He asks Ilse to read his name back to him, twice.
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op1-4 "a1-4" (The Hospice — after dark), line 1 of 4.

trans-unit.source: Buboes in winter. The pestilence is early this year, Doctor. Or it was invited.
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op1-4 "a1-4" (The Hospice — after dark), line 2 of 4.

trans-unit.source: Fevers don’t wait for invitations, Inquisitor.
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op1-4 "a1-4" (The Hospice — after dark), line 3 of 4.

trans-unit.source: In my experience, everything does.
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op1-4 "a1-4" (The Hospice — after dark), line 4 of 4.

trans-unit.source: The Hospice — the table goes still
trans-unit.note: Place caption of failure scene when the patient of op1-1 dies, before the retry prompt "f1-1".

trans-unit.source: Simple work, Kreuzer. Wash your hands. Look at the wounds again. Then do it properly.
trans-unit.note: Failure scene when the patient of op1-1 dies, before the retry prompt "f1-1" (The Hospice — the table goes still), line 1 of 1.

trans-unit.source: The Hospice — the table goes still
trans-unit.note: Place caption of failure scene when the patient of op1-2 dies, before the retry prompt "f1-2".

trans-unit.source: Eleven.
trans-unit.note: Failure scene when the patient of op1-2 dies, before the retry prompt "f1-2" (The Hospice — the table goes still), line 1 of 2.

trans-unit.source: Free the barbs before you pull, not after. Again, Kreuzer. He is not yet cold, and neither are you.
trans-unit.note: Failure scene when the patient of op1-2 dies, before the retry prompt "f1-2" (The Hospice — the table goes still), line 2 of 2.

trans-unit.source: The Hospice — the table goes still
trans-unit.note: Place caption of failure scene when the patient of op1-3 dies, before the retry prompt "f1-3".

trans-unit.source: His pulse was fading, Doctor, and we let it fade. The tincture is there to be used.
trans-unit.note: Failure scene when the patient of op1-3 dies, before the retry prompt "f1-3" (The Hospice — the table goes still), line 1 of 1.

trans-unit.source: The Hospice — the table goes still
trans-unit.note: Place caption of failure scene when the patient of op1-4 dies, before the retry prompt "f1-4".

trans-unit.source: I wrote his name down. I will not write it in the other ledger. Not tonight. Again, Doctor.
trans-unit.note: Failure scene when the patient of op1-4 dies, before the retry prompt "f1-4" (The Hospice — the table goes still), line 1 of 1.

trans-unit.source: The Hospice — the small hours
trans-unit.note: Place caption of failure scene when the patient of op1-5 dies, before the retry prompt "f1-5".

trans-unit.source: It fights, Kreuzer. It is meant to. Brand it only when it opens its eye — and remember the star.
trans-unit.note: Failure scene when the patient of op1-5 dies, before the retry prompt "f1-5" (The Hospice — the small hours), line 1 of 1.

trans-unit.source: Jost the drover swore off dice for good. He broke the promise by Friday, and the stitches held anyway.
trans-unit.note: "Where are they now" line for the patient of op1-1, read after the chapter ends. Narration; wry, not cruel.

trans-unit.source: Pieter kept the arrowhead on a cord round his neck and told the militia it was from a duel.
trans-unit.note: "Where are they now" line for the patient of op1-2, read after the chapter ends. Narration; wry, not cruel.

trans-unit.source: Anno went back to the gunsmith’s bench and now stands to the side of every barrel he proves.
trans-unit.note: "Where are they now" line for the patient of op1-3, read after the chapter ends. Narration; wry, not cruel.

trans-unit.source: Matthis Kolb returned to the Tanners’ Rows, and would speak of the buboes to no one but the hospice cat.
trans-unit.note: "Where are they now" line for the patient of op1-4, read after the chapter ends. Narration; wry, not cruel.

trans-unit.source: Emmerich no longer hears the singing. He sleeps with a candle lit, and nobody at the hospice has the heart to stop him.
trans-unit.note: "Where are they now" line for the patient of op1-5, read after the chapter ends. Narration; wry, not cruel.

trans-unit.note: Patient line on the chart and HUD.

trans-unit.source: Barbed arrow lodged in the left flank; crossbow bolt in the thigh. Raider ambush.
trans-unit.note: Findings paragraph on the patient chart.

trans-unit.note: Operation title (briefing, HUD banner, results, theatre list).

trans-unit.source: Anno, gunsmith’s apprentice
trans-unit.note: Patient line on the chart and HUD.

trans-unit.source: Burst-barrel injury: powder burns across the chest, lead fragments embedded beneath the skin.
trans-unit.note: Findings paragraph on the patient chart.

trans-unit.note: Operation title (briefing, HUD banner, results, theatre list).

trans-unit.note: Patient line on the chart and HUD.

trans-unit.source: Plague buboes, spreading rot and an infested sore. High fever.
trans-unit.note: Findings paragraph on the patient chart.

trans-unit.note: Operation title (briefing, HUD banner, results, theatre list).

trans-unit.source: Emmerich, page-boy
trans-unit.note: Patient line on the chart and HUD.

trans-unit.source: Unknown. Moving marks on the chest. Delirium. “The choir is singing in me.”
trans-unit.note: Findings paragraph on the patient chart.

trans-unit.source: Two deep cuts. Take the Gut Thread and zig-zag across each wound to stitch it.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 1 of 3 of "A Tavern Knife" begins.

trans-unit.source: Cross the wound again and again, moving along it. One smooth stroke earns the best marks.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 1 of 3 of "A Tavern Knife" begins.

trans-unit.source: Blood’s pooled from the cuts. Hold the Leech-Pipe over it to draw it off.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 2 of 3 of "A Tavern Knife" begins.

trans-unit.source: Next time, drain first — you can’t stitch through a pool of blood.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 2 of 3 of "A Tavern Knife" begins.

trans-unit.source: Just nicks left. Brush Saint’s Salve over the small ones — no need for Gut Thread.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 3 of 3 of "A Tavern Knife" begins.

trans-unit.source: The arrow’s barbed. Lancet first — two nicks at the entry wound.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 1 of 2 of "The Barbed Shaft" begins.

trans-unit.source: Then seize it with the Tongs and pull it well clear.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 1 of 2 of "The Barbed Shaft" begins.

trans-unit.source: Then drain and stitch the wound it leaves.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 1 of 2 of "The Barbed Shaft" begins.

trans-unit.source: The bolt in his thigh has no barbs. Tongs, and pull it straight out.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 2 of 2 of "The Barbed Shaft" begins.

trans-unit.source: Quick, clean pulls earn the best marks.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 2 of 2 of "The Barbed Shaft" begins.

trans-unit.source: His pulse is weak already. Hold the Tincture to the flesh to steady him if need be.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 1 of 4 of "Powder Burns" begins.

trans-unit.source: Burns first. Tongs to pluck the black eschar, then Saint’s Salve on the raw flesh.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 1 of 4 of "Powder Burns" begins.

trans-unit.source: Now open him along the inked line with the Lancet. Start at the glowing end.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 2 of 4 of "Powder Burns" begins.

trans-unit.source: There — the shot. Pull each ball out with the Tongs.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 3 of 4 of "Powder Burns" begins.

trans-unit.source: Everything’s clear. Close the incision with the Gut Thread.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 4 of 4 of "Powder Burns" begins.

trans-unit.source: Lance each bubo with a single touch of the Lancet before it bursts.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 1 of 3 of "Pestilent Humours" begins.

trans-unit.source: Then drain the pus and brush Saint’s Salve over it.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 1 of 3 of "Pestilent Humours" begins.

trans-unit.source: Grubs in the sore! The Cautery Brand — hold it on each one until it stops moving.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 2 of 3 of "Pestilent Humours" begins.

trans-unit.source: Don’t linger on bare flesh with the Cautery Brand.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 2 of 3 of "Pestilent Humours" begins.

trans-unit.source: The rot’s spreading. Saint’s Salve on every patch — quickly, it creeps back.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 3 of 3 of "Pestilent Humours" begins.

trans-unit.source: Those sigils are draining him. Trace every stroke with the Cautery Brand to sear them.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 1 of 5 of "The Hour of Matins" begins.

trans-unit.source: Something is moving beneath the skin. We have to open him. The Lancet — along the line.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 2 of 5 of "The Hour of Matins" begins.

trans-unit.source: Saints preserve us… what is that?
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 3 of 5 of "The Hour of Matins" begins.

trans-unit.source: Doctor — if ever there were a time for the Litany, it is now. Draw the star.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 3 of 5 of "The Hour of Matins" begins.

trans-unit.source: It’s gone. Tend the wounds it left.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 4 of 5 of "The Hour of Matins" begins.

trans-unit.source: Everything’s clear. Close the incision with the Gut Thread.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 5 of 5 of "The Hour of Matins" begins.

trans-unit.source: CHAPTER II — THE HOUR OF LAUDS
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-1" (The Timber Road — the Watch’s muster camp, three leagues east of Kessendorf), line 1 of 11.

trans-unit.source: A week later.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-1" (The Timber Road — the Watch’s muster camp, three leagues east of Kessendorf), line 2 of 11.

trans-unit.source: A week after the page-boy, a writ arrives under the Watch’s seal: the hospice’s surgeon is requisitioned for the muster.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-1" (The Timber Road — the Watch’s muster camp, three leagues east of Kessendorf), line 3 of 11.

trans-unit.source: Don’t look at me like that, Doctor. The Inquisitor dines with the Burgomaster on Thursdays. On Fridays, the Burgomaster signs things.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-1" (The Timber Road — the Watch’s muster camp, three leagues east of Kessendorf), line 4 of 11.

trans-unit.source: So Stroh can watch you somewhere with fewer witnesses.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-1" (The Timber Road — the Watch’s muster camp, three leagues east of Kessendorf), line 5 of 11.

trans-unit.source: Fewer? Forty men in this camp, Sister. Forty witnesses. Forty-one with the cook, and I don’t count the cook.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-1" (The Timber Road — the Watch’s muster camp, three leagues east of Kessendorf), line 6 of 11.

trans-unit.source: You count everyone, Captain. You counted the mules.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-1" (The Timber Road — the Watch’s muster camp, three leagues east of Kessendorf), line 7 of 11.

trans-unit.source: The mules keep better order. We clear the Grauwald of raiders before the spring caravans. Two scouts came back from the barrow-fields.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-1" (The Timber Road — the Watch’s muster camp, three leagues east of Kessendorf), line 8 of 11.

trans-unit.source: Something followed them out.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-1" (The Timber Road — the Watch’s muster camp, three leagues east of Kessendorf), line 9 of 11.

trans-unit.source: A gravehound. Claw rakes across his back — and it has left its teeth in him.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-1" (The Timber Road — the Watch’s muster camp, three leagues east of Kessendorf), line 10 of 11.

trans-unit.source: Corpse-eaters carry a venom in their spit. Tomas, isn’t it? Look at me, Tomas. You’ll keep the arm.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-1" (The Timber Road — the Watch’s muster camp, three leagues east of Kessendorf), line 11 of 11.

trans-unit.source: The muster camp — afternoon
trans-unit.note: Place and time caption at the top-left of the scene.

trans-unit.source: Put me down, you long-legged oafs! I can walk! I can… mostly walk.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-2" (The muster camp — afternoon), line 1 of 9.

trans-unit.source: Dwarf prospector. Her crew was working a seam in the hills when it caved in.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-2" (The muster camp — afternoon), line 2 of 9.

trans-unit.source: The rock went black, Doctor. Black as a wet eye, and it had a pulse. It sang when we struck it. Then it burst.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-2" (The muster camp — afternoon), line 3 of 9.

trans-unit.source: Mind her beard, Doctor. Every knot in it is tied for a debt.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-2" (The muster camp — afternoon), line 4 of 9.

trans-unit.source: Nineteen knots. Nine are owed to me, ten I owe. If I die owing ten, my sons pay them, and my sons are idle.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-2" (The muster camp — afternoon), line 5 of 9.

trans-unit.source: There are shards under her skin I can’t see — but the flesh around them is spoiling.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-2" (The muster camp — afternoon), line 6 of 9.

trans-unit.source: Master Haller sent his old Scrying Lens with me. He says you are to break anything else of his first.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-2" (The muster camp — afternoon), line 7 of 9.

trans-unit.source: Dwarf hide’s thicker than yours, lad. You’ll want a strong arm on that thread.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-2" (The muster camp — afternoon), line 8 of 9.

trans-unit.source: Hold still, Mistress Flintvein, and I’ll owe you a knot.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-2" (The muster camp — afternoon), line 9 of 9.

trans-unit.source: The muster camp — night
trans-unit.note: Place and time caption at the top-left of the scene.

trans-unit.source: Orsa sleeps in the supply wagon, snoring like a bellows. The sentries swear it keeps the wolves off.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-3" (The muster camp — night), line 1 of 8.

trans-unit.source: Elf forager. Went to check his snares by the old web-trees. We found him wrapped up like a midwinter ham.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-3" (The muster camp — night), line 2 of 8.

trans-unit.source: …the brood-mother… she kissed me… she was so gentle about it…
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-3" (The muster camp — night), line 3 of 8.

trans-unit.source: Elf skin, Doctor — thin as vellum. It cuts at a breath and bleeds like a spring.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-3" (The muster camp — night), line 4 of 8.

trans-unit.source: The foresters call the great web-spinners brood-mothers. Venom, spreading fast. And these lumps… Saints. She laid in him.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-3" (The muster camp — night), line 5 of 8.

trans-unit.source: My lads won’t fetch water past the web-trees now. They say a brood-mother remembers every face that has seen her.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-3" (The muster camp — night), line 6 of 8.

trans-unit.source: Then fetch my water from somewhere she hasn’t looked, Captain. And more light.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-3" (The muster camp — night), line 7 of 8.

trans-unit.source: The sacs are swelling, Doctor. If they hatch on their own, they’ll scatter.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-3" (The muster camp — night), line 8 of 8.

trans-unit.source: The muster camp — before midnight
trans-unit.note: Place and time caption at the top-left of the scene.

trans-unit.source: Doctor. I have brought you a gift.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-4" (The muster camp — before midnight), line 1 of 10.

trans-unit.source: Two of the Inquisitor’s men drag a thin, grey-robed figure into the light. His chest is a lattice of glowing sigils.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-4" (The muster camp — before midnight), line 2 of 10.

trans-unit.source: A lay-cantor of the Hollow Choir. We took him in the barrow-fields, singing to the dead. Something in the barrows sang back.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-4" (The muster camp — before midnight), line 3 of 10.

trans-unit.source: The moment he began to confess, those marks ignited. He also swallowed something. His masters would rather he burned than spoke.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-4" (The muster camp — before midnight), line 4 of 10.

trans-unit.source: You will keep him alive, Doctor — and awake. I have questions, and the dead are poor at answering them.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-4" (The muster camp — before midnight), line 5 of 10.

trans-unit.source: …He’s dying, Doctor. Whatever else he is, he’s a patient.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-4" (The muster camp — before midnight), line 6 of 10.

trans-unit.source: The cantor’s eyes find Kreuzer’s. Stroh waits, one glove already off.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-4" (The muster camp — before midnight), line 7 of 10. Choice prompt: the player then picks one of 2 replies (ids .o1–.o2).

trans-unit.source: I treat the man on my table, Inquisitor, not your witness. If he needs poppy for the pain, he has poppy.
trans-unit.note: Reply 1 of 2 to the choice at s2-4.007; shown as a menu option, then in the backlog as Kreuzer's line. Sets `cantorMercy` = true.

trans-unit.source: You’ll have him alive and awake, Inquisitor. Keep your men out of my light.
trans-unit.note: Reply 2 of 2 to the choice at s2-4.007; shown as a menu option, then in the backlog as Kreuzer's line. Sets `cantorMercy` = false.

trans-unit.source: Poppy. So the Choir’s man sleeps soft while the city burns its sick. I shall remember whose mercy that was.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-4" (The muster camp — before midnight), line 8 of 10. Variant line: shown only if `cantorMercy` is set.

trans-unit.source: Alive and awake. Good. We understand each other, Doctor — a rarer thing than you know.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-4" (The muster camp — before midnight), line 9 of 10. Variant line: shown only if `cantorMercy` is false.

trans-unit.source: On the table. Now.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-4" (The muster camp — before midnight), line 10 of 10.

trans-unit.source: The muster camp — dawn
trans-unit.note: Place and time caption at the top-left of the scene.

trans-unit.source: Lauds… is sung at dawn… with the muster… under the banner…
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-5" (The muster camp — dawn), line 1 of 10.

trans-unit.source: The dawn muster? That’s now—
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-5" (The muster camp — dawn), line 2 of 10.

trans-unit.source: Across the camp, forty voices sing up the dawn. Beneath them, two more voices begin: one calling, one answering.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-5" (The muster camp — dawn), line 3 of 10.

trans-unit.source: Who keeps the watch before the sun?
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-5" (The muster camp — dawn), line 4 of 10.

trans-unit.source: The one who wakes, and wakes alone.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-5" (The muster camp — dawn), line 5 of 10.

trans-unit.source: Who sings the day when day is done?
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-5" (The muster camp — dawn), line 6 of 10.

trans-unit.source: The one we answer, bone to bone.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-5" (The muster camp — dawn), line 7 of 10.

trans-unit.source: The standard-bearer drops to his knees, the banner falling across him. The hymn falters. The two voices do not.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-5" (The muster camp — dawn), line 8 of 10.

trans-unit.source: Doctor! It’s Jorg — there are two of them in his chest, and each one answers the other!
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-5" (The muster camp — dawn), line 9 of 10.

trans-unit.source: Clear a table. Sister — every instrument we have.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-5" (The muster camp — dawn), line 10 of 10.

trans-unit.source: The muster camp — morning
trans-unit.note: Place and time caption at the top-left of the scene.

trans-unit.source: The singing stops. The standard-bearer breathes. In the flesh over his heart, a single word: LAUDS.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-end" (The muster camp — morning), line 1 of 13.

trans-unit.source: And beside it — Doctor, look. An eye with a stroke through it. The same mark the page-boy carried.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-end" (The muster camp — morning), line 2 of 13.

trans-unit.source: Two of them now. Matins in the city, Lauds in my own camp. Someone is keeping time, Doctor.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-end" (The muster camp — morning), line 3 of 13.

trans-unit.source: Six more hours to the full Office. Prime. Terce. Sext. None. Vespers. Compline.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-end" (The muster camp — morning), line 4 of 13.

trans-unit.source: In the ward tent a wounded pikeman hums the dawn hymn in his sleep. Two notes. Then, from nowhere, the answer.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-end" (The muster camp — morning), line 5 of 13.

trans-unit.source: Doctor Kreuzer.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-end" (The muster camp — morning), line 6 of 13.

trans-unit.source: When that thing screamed, every candle in this tent stopped flickering. The flames stood still. For eight heartbeats.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-end" (The muster camp — morning), line 7 of 13. Variant line: shown only if the Litany was spoken in the preceding operation.

trans-unit.source: I counted.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-end" (The muster camp — morning), line 8 of 13. Variant line: shown only if the Litany was spoken in the preceding operation.

trans-unit.source: …The morning air is very still, Inquisitor.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-end" (The muster camp — morning), line 9 of 13. Variant line: shown only if the Litany was spoken in the preceding operation.

trans-unit.source: I watched your hands while that thing screamed. They shook, Doctor. For once.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-end" (The muster camp — morning), line 10 of 13. Variant line: shown only if the Litany was NOT spoken in the preceding operation.

trans-unit.source: It was a long night, Inquisitor.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-end" (The muster camp — morning), line 11 of 13. Variant line: shown only if the Litany was NOT spoken in the preceding operation.

trans-unit.source: We will speak at length, you and I. After Prime.
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-end" (The muster camp — morning), line 12 of 13.

trans-unit.source: END OF CHAPTER II — THE HOUR OF LAUDS
trans-unit.note: Story scene "s2-end" (The muster camp — morning), line 13 of 13.

trans-unit.source: The muster camp — after the gravehound
trans-unit.note: Place caption of aftermath scene after op2-1 "a2-1".

trans-unit.source: The scout will limp, but he will limp home.
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op2-1 "a2-1" (The muster camp — after the gravehound), line 1 of 3.

trans-unit.source: Forty. Still forty. I am starting to like you, Doctor, and I don’t care for it.
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op2-1 "a2-1" (The muster camp — after the gravehound), line 2 of 3.

trans-unit.source: Every tooth, and not a drop of venom left. Master Haller would pretend not to be impressed.
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op2-1 "a2-1" (The muster camp — after the gravehound), line 3 of 3. Variant line: shown only if the preceding operation's rank was high (high = XS/S, mid = A/B, low = C).

trans-unit.source: The muster camp — the supply wagon
trans-unit.note: Place caption of aftermath scene after op2-2 "a2-2".

trans-unit.source: A strong arm after all. I shall name a mine for you, Doctor. The Kreuzer Deep.
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op2-2 "a2-2" (The muster camp — the supply wagon), line 1 of 4.

trans-unit.source: Is it a good mine?
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op2-2 "a2-2" (The muster camp — the supply wagon), line 2 of 4.

trans-unit.source: It is not dug yet. It will probably be a bad one. The first ones always are.
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op2-2 "a2-2" (The muster camp — the supply wagon), line 3 of 4.

trans-unit.source: Here. One knot, untied. You owe me nothing, and I owe you one.
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op2-2 "a2-2" (The muster camp — the supply wagon), line 4 of 4. Variant line: shown only if the preceding operation's rank was high (high = XS/S, mid = A/B, low = C).

trans-unit.source: The muster camp — after midnight
trans-unit.note: Place caption of aftermath scene after op2-3 "a2-3".

trans-unit.source: Ilvaren wakes asking after his snares. The web-trees are left to the foresters, and to the fire.
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op2-3 "a2-3" (The muster camp — after midnight), line 1 of 3.

trans-unit.source: Forty, and a forager who will never set a snare again. My lads are calling you the spider-cutter.
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op2-3 "a2-3" (The muster camp — after midnight), line 2 of 3.

trans-unit.source: Tell them I have been called worse by better men.
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op2-3 "a2-3" (The muster camp — after midnight), line 3 of 3.

trans-unit.source: The muster camp — the Inquisitor’s tent
trans-unit.note: Place caption of aftermath scene after op2-4 "a2-4".

trans-unit.source: The cantor breathes. The sigils on his chest are ash. Stroh’s men stand at the tent flap and do not let the Doctor leave.
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op2-4 "a2-4" (The muster camp — the Inquisitor’s tent), line 1 of 3.

trans-unit.source: He lives. Good. Now he can tell me who taught him to sing.
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op2-4 "a2-4" (The muster camp — the Inquisitor’s tent), line 2 of 3.

trans-unit.source: He is a patient until he walks out of this tent, Inquisitor. Then he is yours. Not one hour sooner.
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op2-4 "a2-4" (The muster camp — the Inquisitor’s tent), line 3 of 3.

trans-unit.source: The muster camp — the table goes still
trans-unit.note: Place caption of failure scene when the patient of op2-1 dies, before the retry prompt "f2-1".

trans-unit.source: Thirty-nine. …No. Not yet. Doctor, do it again. I’m not writing that number down.
trans-unit.note: Failure scene when the patient of op2-1 dies, before the retry prompt "f2-1" (The muster camp — the table goes still), line 1 of 1.

trans-unit.source: The muster camp — the table goes still
trans-unit.note: Place caption of failure scene when the patient of op2-2 dies, before the retry prompt "f2-2".

trans-unit.source: The shards we could not see were the ones that killed her. Slower with the lens, Doctor.
trans-unit.note: Failure scene when the patient of op2-2 dies, before the retry prompt "f2-2" (The muster camp — the table goes still), line 1 of 1.

trans-unit.source: The muster camp — the table goes still
trans-unit.note: Place caption of failure scene when the patient of op2-3 dies, before the retry prompt "f2-3".

trans-unit.source: The sacs hatched before we lanced them. We know which ones now. Again.
trans-unit.note: Failure scene when the patient of op2-3 dies, before the retry prompt "f2-3" (The muster camp — the table goes still), line 1 of 1.

trans-unit.source: Orsa Flintvein walked back to her diggings with the shards in a lead box and a promise to return the favour.
trans-unit.note: "Where are they now" line for the patient of op2-2, read after the chapter ends. Narration; wry, not cruel.

trans-unit.source: Ilvaren went home to the Grauwald and planted the spider’s thicket with nettles.
trans-unit.note: "Where are they now" line for the patient of op2-3, read after the chapter ends. Narration; wry, not cruel.

trans-unit.source: The lay-cantor’s hymn is written in the Inquisitor’s ledger, in a hand that pressed hard enough to tear the page.
trans-unit.note: "Where are they now" line for the patient of op2-4, read after the chapter ends. Narration; wry, not cruel.

trans-unit.source: Jorg carried the standard again at the next muster. He hums, now, without noticing, and stops when anyone looks.

trans-unit.source: In the winter of the ninth year of the Long Muster, Dr. Kreuzer took up the knife at the Hospice of Saint Ildra in Kessendorf.
trans-unit.note: Chapter-select recap before ch2 ("previously"), sentence 1 of 3. Narration.

trans-unit.source: A page-boy came in with a mark under his skin that sang, and Kreuzer drew the forbidden star to cut the Malison of Matins out of him.
trans-unit.note: Chapter-select recap before ch2 ("previously"), sentence 2 of 3. Narration.

trans-unit.source: Inquisitor Stroh of the Ash Tribunal saw a candle stop flickering, and has not stopped watching since.
trans-unit.note: Chapter-select recap before ch2 ("previously"), sentence 3 of 3. Narration.

trans-unit.source: A lay-cantor of the Hollow Choir
trans-unit.note: Patient line on the chart and HUD.

trans-unit.note: Findings paragraph on the patient chart.

trans-unit.note: Operation title (briefing, HUD banner, results, theatre list).

trans-unit.source: Jorg, standard-bearer
trans-unit.note: Patient line on the chart and HUD.

trans-unit.source: Collapsed during the dawn hymn. Something beneath the sternum is singing.
trans-unit.note: Findings paragraph on the patient chart.

trans-unit.source: The venom first — hold the Tincture on the bite until it takes.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 1 of 3 of "Gravehound" begins.

trans-unit.source: The longer it spreads, the harder it drags on him.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 1 of 3 of "Gravehound" begins.

trans-unit.source: Now the fangs. Tongs — pull each one clear.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 2 of 3 of "Gravehound" begins.

trans-unit.source: Claw rakes. Three deep lines — drain and stitch each.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 3 of 3 of "Gravehound" begins.

trans-unit.source: Rock splinters on the surface first. Tongs.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 1 of 3 of "The Black Seam" begins.

trans-unit.source: Now — the Scrying Lens. Pass it slowly over the flesh; where something hides, it shimmers.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 2 of 3 of "The Black Seam" begins.

trans-unit.source: Hold it still over the shimmer to bring the shard to light, then pull it.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 2 of 3 of "The Black Seam" begins.

trans-unit.source: Clean up the spoiled flesh and any wounds left.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 3 of 3 of "The Black Seam" begins.

trans-unit.source: Venom from two bites. Tincture on each, quickly.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 1 of 4 of "Brood-Mother’s Kiss" begins.

trans-unit.source: The sacs — lance each with one touch, then sear the hatchlings with the Cautery Brand.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 2 of 4 of "Brood-Mother’s Kiss" begins.

trans-unit.source: Mind the ones that are close to hatching.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 2 of 4 of "Brood-Mother’s Kiss" begins.

trans-unit.source: Her brood-cluster — three sacs under one skin.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 3 of 4 of "Brood-Mother’s Kiss" begins.

trans-unit.source: Cut the membrane right around them with the Lancet first, or they’ll wake as one.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 3 of 4 of "Brood-Mother’s Kiss" begins.

trans-unit.source: One more sac, deeper. Use the Scrying Lens to find it, then open it.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 4 of 4 of "Brood-Mother’s Kiss" begins.

trans-unit.source: And he’s taken a fever-bubo from the bite — lance and cleanse it.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 4 of 4 of "Brood-Mother’s Kiss" begins.

trans-unit.source: The poison he swallowed — Tincture, now, or he’s gone before we start.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 1 of 5 of "The Silenced Cantor" begins.

trans-unit.source: Those sigils are burning him from within. Sear each one out — every stroke.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 2 of 5 of "The Silenced Cantor" begins.

trans-unit.source: There — a knot of it round his throat. Every time he hums, it ties itself again.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 3 of 5 of "The Silenced Cantor" begins.

trans-unit.source: Burn it out between the verses.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 3 of 5 of "The Silenced Cantor" begins.

trans-unit.source: The hexfire burns. Pluck the eschar, then Saint’s Salve on them.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 4 of 5 of "The Silenced Cantor" begins.

trans-unit.source: Maggots in an old sore — the Tribunal’s cells are filthy. Cautery Brand.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 5 of 5 of "The Silenced Cantor" begins.

trans-unit.source: We have to open him — along the line, Doctor.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 1 of 4 of "The Hour of Lauds" begins.

trans-unit.source: A choir! Those lights are its Voices — hold the Cautery Brand on each as it circles.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 2 of 4 of "The Hour of Lauds" begins.

trans-unit.source: Silence all of them and its heart will be bare.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 2 of 4 of "The Hour of Lauds" begins.

trans-unit.source: It’s done. Tend what it left of him.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 3 of 4 of "The Hour of Lauds" begins.

trans-unit.source: Close him up. Gently — he has a banner to carry.
trans-unit.note: Assistant callout when phase 4 of 4 of "The Hour of Lauds" begins.

trans-unit.source: Venom: hold the Tincture on the bite itself until the poison is drawn.

trans-unit.note: Tutorial prompt, first shown in op2-2. Keep {TOKENS} verbatim: they become key/button glyphs. Imperative, one instruction.

trans-unit.source: What the Lens reveals must still be pulled — Tongs, once it shows.
trans-unit.note: Tutorial prompt, first shown in op2-2. Keep {TOKENS} verbatim: they become key/button glyphs. Imperative, one instruction.

trans-unit.source: Egg sacs: lance each before it hatches, then brand what spills out.
trans-unit.note: Tutorial prompt, first shown in op2-3. Keep {TOKENS} verbatim: they become key/button glyphs. Imperative, one instruction.

trans-unit.source: The hospice — the examining room
trans-unit.note: Place caption of aftermath scene after op3-1 "a3-1".

trans-unit.source: Liesl wakes with a bandage like a crown and asks whether she may keep the bits of horn. Her mother says no. Kreuzer says yes.
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op3-1 "a3-1" (The hospice — the examining room), line 1 of 3.

trans-unit.source: Two buds, cut clean. And two sigils seared away beneath them, where no certificate will mention them.
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op3-1 "a3-1" (The hospice — the examining room), line 2 of 3.

trans-unit.source: The certificate mentions a natural growth, Inquisitor. I removed it.
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op3-1 "a3-1" (The hospice — the examining room), line 3 of 3.

trans-unit.source: The hospice — the steps
trans-unit.note: Place caption of aftermath scene after op3-2 "a3-2".

trans-unit.source: Kaspar’s doublet goes into a basin, a scrap at a time. Ilse counts them twice and matches every thread to the hole it came from.
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op3-2 "a3-2" (The hospice — the steps), line 1 of 4.

trans-unit.source: Every scrap, Doctor. He’ll not be burning by Vespers. He may be dancing by Terce.
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op3-2 "a3-2" (The hospice — the steps), line 2 of 4. Variant line: shown only if the preceding operation's rank was high (high = XS/S, mid = A/B, low = C).

trans-unit.source: I pray that was every scrap. We’ll know by Vespers, if he’s burning.
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op3-2 "a3-2" (The hospice — the steps), line 3 of 4. Variant line: shown only if the preceding operation's rank was mid or low (high = XS/S, mid = A/B, low = C).

trans-unit.source: Next! Three off the mill cart, Doctor, and the cart’s coming back for more.
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op3-2 "a3-2" (The hospice — the steps), line 4 of 4.

trans-unit.source: The hospice — night
trans-unit.note: Place caption of aftermath scene after op3-3 "a3-3".

trans-unit.source: Ute Brandt goes home lighter by a quarter-pound of lead, which Ilse weighs, wraps, and labels for the Founders’ Guild.
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op3-3 "a3-3" (The hospice — night), line 1 of 3.

trans-unit.source: Put it in the privy basket. The Guild may send a clerk to collect its property.
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op3-3 "a3-3" (The hospice — night), line 2 of 3.

trans-unit.source: I have already written the receipt, Master. “One quarter-pound of lead, lightly used.”
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op3-3 "a3-3" (The hospice — night), line 3 of 3.

trans-unit.source: The hospice — the steps, evening
trans-unit.note: Place caption of aftermath scene after op3-4 "a3-4".

trans-unit.source: Jannik, Old Rudi and Wenzel lie in a row on the hospice steps, wrapped in one blanket, arguing about whose fault the magazine was.
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op3-4 "a3-4" (The hospice — the steps, evening), line 1 of 3.

trans-unit.source: Three off the table and three still talking. That’s a good count for the Kilnrows.
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op3-4 "a3-4" (The hospice — the steps, evening), line 2 of 3.

trans-unit.source: Keep them talking, Captain. A man complaining is a man breathing.
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op3-4 "a3-4" (The hospice — the steps, evening), line 3 of 3.

trans-unit.source: The Iron Bridge — the Watch hut
trans-unit.note: Place caption of aftermath scene after op3-5 "a3-5".

trans-unit.source: Berthold wakes to find his leg gone and his cart-horse tethered outside the window, which he says is the right way round.
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op3-5 "a3-5" (The Iron Bridge — the Watch hut), line 1 of 3.

trans-unit.source: A peg and a cushion, you said. I’ll hold you to the cushion, Doctor.
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op3-5 "a3-5" (The Iron Bridge — the Watch hut), line 2 of 3.

trans-unit.source: The council has sent a clerk to ask who will pay for the bridge-chain he bent. I sent the clerk away. Twice.
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op3-5 "a3-5" (The Iron Bridge — the Watch hut), line 3 of 3.

trans-unit.source: The quarantine side — the Penny Stair
trans-unit.note: Place caption of aftermath scene after op3-6 "a3-6".

trans-unit.source: Forty-one worms, whole, in a jar. Gottfried the pie-man is asked to look at it, and does, and is quiet for a while.
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op3-6 "a3-6" (The quarantine side — the Penny Stair), line 1 of 3.

trans-unit.source: Eel. They told me it was eel.
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op3-6 "a3-6" (The quarantine side — the Penny Stair), line 2 of 3.

trans-unit.source: Then someone owes Frieda an apology, Gottfried, and you owe the city a new recipe.
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op3-6 "a3-6" (The quarantine side — the Penny Stair), line 3 of 3.

trans-unit.source: The quarantine ward — before dawn
trans-unit.note: Place caption of aftermath scene after op3-7 "a3-7".

trans-unit.source: Mother Agathe of the Grey Beguines sits up at the fourth bell and demands her beads, her boots, and a list of the other sick.
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op3-7 "a3-7" (The quarantine ward — before dawn), line 1 of 2.

trans-unit.source: You lance like a Beguine, boy. That is the highest praise I have. Now go and do it to someone else.
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op3-7 "a3-7" (The quarantine ward — before dawn), line 2 of 2.

trans-unit.source: The quarantine ward — dawn
trans-unit.note: Place caption of aftermath scene after op3-8 "a3-8".

trans-unit.source: Brother Ansgar sleeps face-down with his hands open. The nails are in a bowl beside him. He has not asked for them back.
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op3-8 "a3-8" (The quarantine ward — dawn), line 1 of 3.

trans-unit.source: He asked me whether a debt can be paid by someone else. I told him the Order thinks so. I hope it does.
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op3-8 "a3-8" (The quarantine ward — dawn), line 2 of 3.

trans-unit.source: Let him sleep, Sister. We can argue theology when his back has closed.
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op3-8 "a3-8" (The quarantine ward — dawn), line 3 of 3.

trans-unit.source: The Hall of Records — morning
trans-unit.note: Place caption of aftermath scene after op3-10 "a3-10".

trans-unit.source: The Registrar’s skin is clean. The roll of the dead is the right length again, and every name on it had a family to miss it.
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op3-10 "a3-10" (The Hall of Records — morning), line 1 of 4.

trans-unit.source: I read the names of strangers, Doctor. People who had not died. Did they… will they?
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op3-10 "a3-10" (The Hall of Records — morning), line 2 of 4.

trans-unit.source: Not from anything you read, Registrar. Go home. Read something with a happy ending.
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op3-10 "a3-10" (The Hall of Records — morning), line 3 of 4.

trans-unit.source: The names stopped when you touched him, Doctor. I noticed. I notice things.
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op3-10 "a3-10" (The Hall of Records — morning), line 4 of 4.

trans-unit.source: The hospice — past midnight
trans-unit.note: Place caption of aftermath scene after op3-9 "a3-9".

trans-unit.source: The Inquisitor sits with a cloth to his jaw and his tooth in a twist of paper, which he pockets like evidence.
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op3-9 "a3-9" (The hospice — past midnight), line 1 of 4.

trans-unit.source: That was… gentle, Doctor. I had been told barbers enjoy it. I shall have to revise the Tribunal’s view of your trade.
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op3-9 "a3-9" (The hospice — past midnight), line 2 of 4. Variant line: shown only if the preceding operation's rank was high (high = XS/S, mid = A/B, low = C).

trans-unit.source: The root came out in two pieces. So, very nearly, did I. We shall say no more of it.
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op3-9 "a3-9" (The hospice — past midnight), line 3 of 4. Variant line: shown only if the preceding operation's rank was mid or low (high = XS/S, mid = A/B, low = C).

trans-unit.source: Rinse with salt, Inquisitor. And ask your questions in daylight.
trans-unit.note: Aftermath scene after op3-9 "a3-9" (The hospice — past midnight), line 4 of 4.

trans-unit.source: Next — Chapter III: Prime and Terce
trans-unit.note: Place caption of chapter iii teaser read after the demo end card "teaser-3".

trans-unit.source: Foundry smoke lies so thick over the Kilnrows that the lamplighters go out at noon.
trans-unit.note: Chapter III teaser read after the demo end card "teaser-3" (Next — Chapter III: Prime and Terce), line 1 of 6.

trans-unit.source: At dusk the river bridges are raised, and the Watch asks every child at the gate to show its forehead.
trans-unit.note: Chapter III teaser read after the demo end card "teaser-3" (Next — Chapter III: Prime and Terce), line 2 of 6.

trans-unit.source: The Guild will put your licence to the vote, boy. I stood in that hall once before. I can stand in it again.
trans-unit.note: Chapter III teaser read after the demo end card "teaser-3" (Next — Chapter III: Prime and Terce), line 3 of 6.

trans-unit.source: Doctor, there is a girl at the door with two nubs of horn in her hair, and her mother is praying.
trans-unit.note: Chapter III teaser read after the demo end card "teaser-3" (Next — Chapter III: Prime and Terce), line 4 of 6.

trans-unit.source: On the steps of the Hall of Records, a registrar reads the roll of the dead aloud, and the names keep coming.
trans-unit.note: Chapter III teaser read after the demo end card "teaser-3" (Next — Chapter III: Prime and Terce), line 5 of 6.

trans-unit.source: I said we would speak after Prime, Doctor. It is nearly after Prime.
trans-unit.note: Chapter III teaser read after the demo end card "teaser-3" (Next — Chapter III: Prime and Terce), line 6 of 6.

trans-unit.source: The Watch marched to the barrow-fields with Kreuzer as its surgeon, and brought home a cantor whose chest was a lattice of sigils.
trans-unit.note: Chapter-select recap before ch3 ("previously"), sentence 1 of 3. Narration.

trans-unit.source: At the muster, the Malison of Lauds sang through its host until Kreuzer silenced it — some say by the Litany, in front of witnesses.
trans-unit.note: Chapter-select recap before ch3 ("previously"), sentence 2 of 3. Narration.

trans-unit.source: Stroh has promised they will speak after Prime. It is after Prime.
trans-unit.note: Chapter-select recap before ch3 ("previously"), sentence 3 of 3. Narration.

trans-unit.source: Berthold
Gottfried, pie-man
Mother Agathe
Registrar Tallert
Kessendorf — Hollow Night, after Compline
trans-unit.note: Place caption of the perfect end: failure scene when the finale (op5-9) is lost, before the retry prompt "s5-end-perfect".

trans-unit.source: The last sigil on the Precentor’s heart turns, and the clock-face of eight Hours is complete.
trans-unit.note: The Perfect End: failure scene when the finale (op5-9) is lost, before the retry prompt "s5-end-perfect" (Kessendorf — Hollow Night, after Compline), line 1 of 18.

trans-unit.source: He does not die. He only stops. And the silence goes out of him like a tide.
trans-unit.note: The Perfect End: failure scene when the finale (op5-9) is lost, before the retry prompt "s5-end-perfect" (Kessendorf — Hollow Night, after Compline), line 2 of 18.

trans-unit.source: Now let your servant depart in peace.
trans-unit.note: The Perfect End: failure scene when the finale (op5-9) is lost, before the retry prompt "s5-end-perfect" (Kessendorf — Hollow Night, after Compline), line 3 of 18.

trans-unit.source: It reaches the crypt first. Orsa sits down on the stone floor with her pick across her knees and closes her eyes.
trans-unit.note: The Perfect End: failure scene when the finale (op5-9) is lost, before the retry prompt "s5-end-perfect" (Kessendorf — Hollow Night, after Compline), line 4 of 18.

trans-unit.source: Then the stair. Then the street. Then the ward.
trans-unit.note: The Perfect End: failure scene when the finale (op5-9) is lost, before the retry prompt "s5-end-perfect" (Kessendorf — Hollow Night, after Compline), line 5 of 18.

trans-unit.source: Doctor — the patients. Their breathing. It’s slowing, all of them, together, like one—
trans-unit.note: The Perfect End: failure scene when the finale (op5-9) is lost, before the retry prompt "s5-end-perfect" (Kessendorf — Hollow Night, after Compline), line 6 of 18.

trans-unit.source: She does not finish the word. She lies down on the ward floor beside the cots, very neatly, as if she means to rest a moment.
trans-unit.note: The Perfect End: failure scene when the finale (op5-9) is lost, before the retry prompt "s5-end-perfect" (Kessendorf — Hollow Night, after Compline), line 7 of 18.

trans-unit.source: The Watch on the Penny Stair lowers its pikes. Mauer counts his men once, and does not reach the end of the count.
trans-unit.note: The Perfect End: failure scene when the finale (op5-9) is lost, before the retry prompt "s5-end-perfect" (Kessendorf — Hollow Night, after Compline), line 8 of 18.

trans-unit.source: The drover at the Crooked Goose puts down his dice. The girl with the horn-buds sleeps, and her mother sleeps beside her.
trans-unit.note: The Perfect End: failure scene when the finale (op5-9) is lost, before the retry prompt "s5-end-perfect" (Kessendorf — Hollow Night, after Compline), line 9 of 18.

trans-unit.source: Every candle in Kessendorf stands perfectly still, and then, one by one, goes quietly out.
trans-unit.note: The Perfect End: failure scene when the finale (op5-9) is lost, before the retry prompt "s5-end-perfect" (Kessendorf — Hollow Night, after Compline), line 10 of 18.

trans-unit.source: Hush the ward, and hush the street; / sleep is kind, and death is sweet.
trans-unit.note: The Perfect End: failure scene when the finale (op5-9) is lost, before the retry prompt "s5-end-perfect" (Kessendorf — Hollow Night, after Compline), line 11 of 18.

trans-unit.source: Only Kreuzer is awake. The Litany keeps him, the way it kept every patient he ever held together with it.
trans-unit.note: The Perfect End: failure scene when the finale (op5-9) is lost, before the retry prompt "s5-end-perfect" (Kessendorf — Hollow Night, after Compline), line 12 of 18.

trans-unit.source: Aurel. Wake them. You were a surgeon once. You swore to it.
trans-unit.note: The Perfect End: failure scene when the finale (op5-9) is lost, before the retry prompt "s5-end-perfect" (Kessendorf — Hollow Night, after Compline), line 13 of 18.

trans-unit.source: I am keeping it, Doctor. No more pain. No more plague. No more surgeons. It is the perfect end.
trans-unit.note: The Perfect End: failure scene when the finale (op5-9) is lost, before the retry prompt "s5-end-perfect" (Kessendorf — Hollow Night, after Compline), line 14 of 18.

trans-unit.source: It is the end. It is not perfect. There is no such thing as a perfect end. There is only the next patient.
trans-unit.note: The Perfect End: failure scene when the finale (op5-9) is lost, before the retry prompt "s5-end-perfect" (Kessendorf — Hollow Night, after Compline), line 15 of 18.

trans-unit.source: He picks up the lancet. His hands are the only moving thing in the city.
trans-unit.note: The Perfect End: failure scene when the finale (op5-9) is lost, before the retry prompt "s5-end-perfect" (Kessendorf — Hollow Night, after Compline), line 16 of 18.

trans-unit.source: Again. From the first Hour.
trans-unit.note: The Perfect End: failure scene when the finale (op5-9) is lost, before the retry prompt "s5-end-perfect" (Kessendorf — Hollow Night, after Compline), line 17 of 18.

trans-unit.source: THE PERFECT END — the Office is complete. Try the operation again.
trans-unit.note: The Perfect End: failure scene when the finale (op5-9) is lost, before the retry prompt "s5-end-perfect" (Kessendorf — Hollow Night, after Compline), line 18 of 18.

trans-unit.source: In the rain of the Vennmark, Kreuzer kept Mauer’s men alive through Sext and None, in tents that never stopped leaking.
trans-unit.note: Chapter-select recap before ch5 ("previously"), sentence 1 of 3. Narration.

trans-unit.source: The council roll showed Stroh’s charter had lapsed at the new year; what the Tribunal did since, it did on nothing.
trans-unit.note: Chapter-select recap before ch5 ("previously"), sentence 2 of 3. Narration.
